source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking
finding: Closest AI replication of Jansson and Smith: designers sketched chatbot avatars after seeing a fixed example avatar. A Midjourney group fixated more on the example than a no-help group, and more than a Google Image Search group.
numbers: N=60 between-participants, 3 groups (no help, image search, Midjourney), equal size. Fixation score = share of the example's features copied. Bayesian binomial model: GenAI +0.32 (89% CI .11 to .55, BF 124); image search +0.27 (CI .05 to .49, BF 42.48). Two blind raters counted features.
limits: Human designers (students with visual design experience), sketching, one example, image generator not LLM text. Posterior means are on a log-odds scale.
agent_relevance: Outside inspiration from a generator raises copying of the first example. An agent that sees a model-made first attempt in context will likely copy its features. Supports S3 fresh contexts: do not show the earlier attempt when asking for a new one.

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking (fluency, variety, originality)
finding: Despite the abstract saying AI users made fewer, less varied, less original ideas, the body shows the divergent-thinking losses were small and uncertain, except fluency. Image search hurt fluency more than GenAI did.
numbers: Fluency total effect: GenAI -0.21; image search -0.49 (89% CI -0.9 to -0.10, BF 46.62, 98% posterior prob. negative). Variety total effect GenAI -0.29 (CI -0.75 to .16, 86% prob. negative, BF 5.93). Originality GenAI -0.03 (CI -.06 to .00), called negligible by the authors.
limits: Abstract and body differ in strength. Effects other than fixation are weak. Single task (chatbot avatar), short time limit.
agent_relevance: Do not claim that AI inspiration reduces variety; claim only the fixation effect is well supported. Treat variety loss as a hypothesis to test on our agent.

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking (fixation displacement)
finding: Qualitative finding: with AI images, fixation moved from the researcher's example to the AI's latest images. Participants anchored on whatever the generator showed last.
numbers: Seen in sketch sequence boards (Fig. 13); no count given in the text read.
limits: Qualitative; small sample.
agent_relevance: In a loop, the newest output becomes the new anchor. Fresh context per attempt removes this ratchet; an operator that shows only a summary of prior attempts may reduce it.

source: Jansson and Smith (1991) Design fixation, as described in Wadinambiarachchi et al. 2024
finding: Founding study as summarised by the CHI 2024 paper: a fixation group saw an example with flaws, a control group did not. Fixation groups copied example features, and later work found less flexibility and originality in their designs.
numbers: Not read directly; no figures taken from the original.
limits: Second-hand description only. Open the original before citing numbers.
agent_relevance: Defines the paradigm our agent test should copy: example vs no-example, count copied features.

source: Wenger and Kenett (2025) We're Different, We're the Same: Creative Homogeneity Across LLMs
finding: 22 LLMs asked the same creativity prompts (AUT, Forward Flow, DAT) gave far more similar answers to each other than 102 humans did, even though average originality was similar.
numbers: Mean population variability (cosine distance): AUT LLM 0.459 vs human 0.738; FF 0.534 vs 0.835; DAT 0.665 vs 0.819. Effect sizes 2.2, 2.0, 1.4. Humans: 114 recruited, 102 kept.
quote: LLM responses are much more similar to other LLM responses than human responses are to each other.
limits: Table columns read from garbled text (LLM first, human second). Humans from Prolific.
agent_relevance: Models fixate on the same default ideas across runs and across models. Using a second model as a fresh sampler gives less diversity than hoped.

source: Wenger and Kenett (2025) system-prompt and family tests
finding: Changing the system prompt shifted individual scores slightly but not population diversity. Same-family (Llama) models were only slightly more alike than unrelated ones.
numbers: Table 7: creative vs neutral vs uncreative system prompts changed originality slightly; variability stayed far below humans. Family difference not statistically significant.
limits: Subset of models; mostly AUT.
agent_relevance: Prompt-level 'be creative' instructions are not enough; need structural diversity such as independent contexts with different starting constraints.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models
finding: Intra-model repetition: sampling one model many times on open-ended prompts gives near-duplicates even at top-p 0.9 and temperature 1.0.
numbers: Infinity-Chat: 26K real open-ended queries, 31,250 human labels (25 annotators each). 50 responses per model on 100 queries, 70+ models studied (25 detailed). In 79% of cases average pairwise similarity within a model exceeds 0.8 (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small).
limits: Embedding similarity is only a proxy for idea sameness.
agent_relevance: Repeated sampling from the same prompt yields the same idea again. Best-of-N over identical prompts wastes budget; fresh contexts must differ in more than the seed.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (decoding fixes)
finding: Min-p decoding with temperature 2.0 reduces extreme repetition but does not remove it.
numbers: With min-p 0.1, temp 2.0: 81% of response pairs still above 0.7 similarity and 61.2% above 0.8.
limits: One embedding model; creative queries.
agent_relevance: Randomness knobs do not fix fixation; change the input, not the sampler.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (inter-model)
finding: Different models and vendors converge: strong cross-model overlap, sometimes long verbatim spans.
numbers: Average pairwise similarity across models 71% to 82%. DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max-2025-01-25 0.82; DeepSeek-V3 vs gpt-4o-2024-11-20 0.81. Across 42 models within-prompt similarity averaged 0.821 vs 0.781 across paraphrases of the prompt.
limits: Causes unknown (shared data or synthetic data suggested by authors).
agent_relevance: Paraphrasing the prompt barely lowers similarity (0.821 to 0.781), so rewording is a weak defence against fixation. Our correlated-error finding (gap 08) fits.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (judges and reward models)
finding: LMs, reward models and LM judges agree less with human ratings when annotators disagree among themselves.
numbers: Correlations computed on full set and on subsets by rater disagreement (Shannon entropy over 25 labels); 6 reward models, 4 LM judges tested. Correlation values not extracted.
limits: Details not extracted.
agent_relevance: A judge step cannot be trusted to rank diverse ideas; the program (not the model) should pick by a check or by dissimilarity.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: Over-generating ideas with an LLM agent saturates: duplicates take over as the pool grows.
numbers: 4000 seed ideas per topic; with cosine threshold 0.8 (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) only about 200 (about 5%) were non-duplicate; the share of new non-duplicates keeps falling and the pool plateaus.
limits: 7 NLP research topics; the 0.8 threshold chosen by manual inspection.
agent_relevance: Scaling samples hits a ceiling set by fixation on a mode. Set a stop rule on novelty rate, not on count.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? (human vs AI novelty)
finding: Blind expert review: AI ideas judged more novel than expert human ideas, with weaker feasibility; human reranking helped slightly.
numbers: Novelty means: human 4.84 (N=49), AI 5.64 (N=49), AI + human rerank 5.81 (N=49); p<0.05. 79 reviewers from 32 institutions; 100+ NLP researchers wrote ideas. LLM self-evaluation was unreliable.
limits: Novelty judged by experts at idea stage, no execution.
agent_relevance: High novelty per idea can coexist with low diversity across ideas. Measure both; do not use the LLM to pick winners.

source: Doshi and Hauser (2024) Generative AI enhances creativity but reduces the diversity of novel content
finding: Humans who got one or five GPT-4 story ideas wrote better stories, but the stories were more like the AI idea and more like each other: an example-induced fixation effect at group level.
numbers: N=293 writers, 600 evaluators. Novelty +5.4% (1 idea) and +8.1% (5 ideas, b=0.311, p<0.001); usefulness +3.7% and +9.0%. Similarity to the AI idea +5.2% (b=4.29, p<0.001; human-only mean 82.85) and +5.0%. Low-creativity (low DAT) writers gained up to 10.7% novelty.
limits: Short 8-sentence stories; similarity by embeddings; one prompt set.
agent_relevance: Examples raise the individual floor but narrow the group. For an agent: examples are good inside one run, harmful across a pool of parallel runs.

source: Padmakumar and He (2023) Does Writing with Language Models Reduce Content Diversity?
finding: Co-writing with a feedback-tuned model (InstructGPT) made essays more alike; co-writing with the base model (GPT-3 davinci) showed no significant effect.
numbers: 38 Upwork writers in 3 groups (solo, GPT-3, InstructGPT). InstructGPT group had lower lexical and key-point diversity. Model wrote about 32-36% of characters; acceptance of suggestions about 70%.
limits: Small sample, one argumentative task. The base-model null may be a power issue.
agent_relevance: Alignment tuning is a likely cause of the fixed mode. Routing some steps through a less-tuned sampler may widen coverage.

source: Mohammadi (2024) Creativity Has Left the Chat: The Price of Debiasing Language Models
finding: Aligned Llama-2 shows lower token entropy, tight embedding clusters and attractor states compared with its base model.
numbers: Three experiments on Llama-2 base vs chat. Aligned outputs formed four distinct clusters in embedding space; base model had higher mean token entropy. Exact entropy values not readable in extracted text.
limits: Single model family; marketing-copy prompts.
agent_relevance: Mode attraction is built in by alignment; example fixation in context stacks on top of it.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
finding: Asking the model to list several answers with their probabilities in one prompt raises diversity without training.
numbers: Creative writing diversity 1.6 to 2.1 times direct prompting; human-rated quality +25.7%; recovers 66.8% of the base model's diversity; Tulu-70B diversity +182.6% over direct at final stage. Larger models gain more (GPT-4.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro).
limits: Diversity by embedding score; some variants lose quality, VS-CoT keeps it.
agent_relevance: A cheap in-prompt scaffold for a wide state: ask for k candidates with probabilities below a threshold. Tunable by the threshold.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity (human study)
finding: Human raters confirmed more diverse outputs with verbalized sampling than with direct prompting or sequence listing.
numbers: 90 Prolific annotators (30 per task), 90 pairs per task, 4-point scale. Diversity: poem direct 1.90, sequence 2.07, VS 2.39; story 2.74, 2.76, 3.06; joke 1.83, 2.93, 3.01. Agreement 0.49 to 0.87.
limits: Judged style, plot, setup, not idea novelty.
agent_relevance: Sequence listing alone gains little on poems and stories, so the probability framing matters, not just asking for many.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity (dials)
finding: Diversity rises as the stated probability threshold falls and as the number of candidates k rises; baseline prompting loses diversity after SFT, DPO and RLVR.
numbers: Fig 3(g-i) threshold sweep; Section F.2 k sweep; Figure 4 across Tulu stages. Numbers read from text, not plots.
limits: Plot values not read.
agent_relevance: Use the threshold as a dial in the schema's breadth slot.

source: Jiang et al. NoveltyBench (2025) Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity
finding: Frontier models give fewer than 3 distinct answers in 10 samples on prompts built to have many valid answers; larger models are worse than smaller ones.
numbers: 1,100 prompts (100 curated, 1,000 from WildChat); 20 models; distinct_k and cumulative utility metrics. Gemma 2-2B and Llama 3.2-1B were among the most diverse. Human baseline: 8 authors per curated prompt.
limits: Equivalence classes by a classifier (79% accuracy vs human labels). Author list not checked.
agent_relevance: Bigger and better on single-answer benchmarks does not mean wider. Do not assume a stronger model avoids fixation.

source: Jiang et al. NoveltyBench (2025) Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity (mitigations)
finding: In-context regeneration (show the model its earlier answers and ask for something different) lifts Claude-3 Opus, GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Pro to about human-level diversity. Paraphrasing and system prompts give little.
numbers: 8 generations per prompt on 100 curated prompts; GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Pro exceed human cumulative utility. More reasoning effort in OpenAI o-series gave less diverse output.
quote: asking a model for "creative outputs" does not work very well
limits: Three models only.
agent_relevance: Here prior outputs in context HELP, because they are framed as things to avoid. This differs from Jansson-Smith, where the example was neutral. Test both framings: 'avoid these' vs 'here is one'.

source: Zhao et al. (2021) Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models
finding: Older mechanistic analogue of example fixation: GPT-3 copies the label that is most common or most recent among the in-context examples.
numbers: Prompt 'P P P N' made nearly 90% of predictions Negative though 3 of 4 examples were Positive. In 4-shot LAMA the model over-predicted answers from examples 1 to 4 by 8.5%, 8.3%, 14.3% and 16.1%. SST-2 4-shot GPT-3 2.7B accuracy ranged 54.3% to 93.4% across example orders. Contextual calibration gained up to 30.0% absolute.
limits: GPT-3 and GPT-2 era; classification tasks.
agent_relevance: Position in context matters: the last-shown example weighs most. If an example must be shown, randomise order across runs.

source: Laban et al. (2025) LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: Models that commit to an early guess in a multi-turn chat keep relying on it and do worse than when given the full task at once.
numbers: 15 LLMs, 200,000+ simulated conversations, 6 tasks; average drop 39% (abstract) or 35% (Fig. 1) from single-turn to sharded multi-turn; aptitude -15%, unreliability +112%. CONCAT (all info at once) matched FULL.
quote: LLMs often make assumptions in early turns and prematurely attempt to generate final solutions
limits: Underspecified-task setting, not ideation; user simulator.
agent_relevance: Direct support for S3: restart in a fresh context with all the facts rather than continue a chat with a wrong early attempt.

source: Laban et al. (2025) LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation (recap and snowball)
finding: Restating all information in the last turn (RECAP) or at every turn (SNOWBALL) recovers some, not all, of the loss.
numbers: Table 2, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini: SNOWBALL reduces the FULL-to-SHARDED deterioration by 15-20%; RECAP does better but needs to know the last turn; both stay below FULL and CONCAT.
limits: Two models, four tasks.
agent_relevance: A recap is a partial fix; a clean restart with a compact statement of facts (our S3) should do at least as well. Test it.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
finding: Many independent samples cover far more problems than one when a verifier picks the right one. Independent draws partly avoid shared fixation.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct: 15.9% with 1 sample to 56% with 250 samples, above single-sample SOTA 43%. Coverage grows roughly log-linearly. Without verifiers, majority vote and reward models plateau.
limits: Verifiable domains. Samples share a prompt, so Hivemind-style duplication limits gains on open-ended tasks.
agent_relevance: Breadth only pays with a check. Give each sample a different starting constraint so draws are not copies.

source: Lou and Sun (2024) Anchoring Bias in Large Language Models: An Experimental Study
finding: Models are pulled by a number or hint placed in the prompt (anchoring). Stronger models were more consistently anchored than GPT-3.5.
numbers: GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5 tested; of the 11 exceptions to anchoring, 9 came from GPT-3.5. Chain-of-thought, Thoughts of Principles, Ignoring Anchor Hints and Reflection did not effectively reduce the bias. A Both-Anchor strategy (opposing anchors) brought GPT-4 near the benchmark on some questions.
limits: Numeric estimation, not ideation; full tables not extracted.
agent_relevance: Telling the model to ignore an anchor fails. Giving two opposed anchors worked partly: for ideas, show contrasting examples, not one.

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2024) Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models
finding: On the Divergent Association Task GPT-4 beats the average human, but the top humans beat every model, and models repeat the same words.
numbers: Human sample about 100,000. GPT-4-turbo put 'ocean' in over 90% of word sets; GPT-4 used 'microscope' in 70% and 'elephant' in 60%; most common human words were 'car' 1.4%, 'dog' 1.2%.
limits: DAT measures word distance, not design ideas.
agent_relevance: Average scores hide mode fixation. Track repeated-item frequency as a fixation meter.

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2024) Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models (temperature and strategy prompts)
finding: Higher temperature and a named strategy in the prompt raise DAT score and cut repetition.
numbers: GPT-4, n=500 per temperature (0.5, 1.0, 1.5); highest gave mean 85.6, above 72% of humans. Prompt adding 'varying etymology' beat the plain instruction for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4; thesaurus strategy also beat it for GPT-4.
limits: One model for temperature.
agent_relevance: A concrete strategy hint (a different route) beats generic 'be creative'. Fits our operator idea: name a distinct angle per fresh run.

source: Davis et al., Creative Sketching Partner, cited in Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024)
finding: Older AI system built to reduce design fixation: an AI partner that shows sketches meant to push designers away from fixation.
numbers: Not read; only mentioned in the CHI 2024 paper.
limits: Second-hand mention only. Year approximate.
agent_relevance: Prior art for an AI counter-fixation partner; follow up if we want a historical comparison.

source: Hoggenmueller et al., cited in Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024)
finding: Cited as exploring text-to-image tools to overcome design fixation in robotic artefact ideation.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Second-hand mention only.
agent_relevance: Lead for a positive-use study; check if it gives counts.
